activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Olivier was at Grandma's house. His little bunny was gone. "Where can bunny be?" he asked.

He looked under the big bed. No bunny. He looked in the toy box. No bunny. Then he saw the kitty cat. The kitty was pulling something with her paws. It was a string. Bunny was at the other end of the string!

"Naughty kitty," said Grandma, smiling. "She pulled bunny all the way under the chair."

Olivier gave the string a little tug. Bunny slid out across the floor. "Bunny!" Olivier called. He hugged bunny tight.

Later, Olivier pulled his toy train by its string. The train followed him all the way to the door. Pull the string, and the toy comes along. What else could he pull next?

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Max was at school. It was cooking day. He wanted to make bread for Mom and Dad and Baby Sam.

Teacher Mia put flour in a big bowl. Max poured in warm water. He mixed and mixed. But the dough stayed flat and stiff. "It won't puff," said Max. His tummy felt sad and hungry.

Teacher Mia laughed. "We forgot the magic dust. Yeast!" Max sprinkled it in. They mixed again. Then they waited. They waited for Mom, and Dad, and Baby Sam, and the yeast.

The dough grew big. It grew and grew. It puffed up like a cloud. "Look!" said Max. "One little pinch made it big!"

Teacher Mia put the bread in the oven. Max watched from far away. Soon the bread was brown and warm.

At home, Max gave the bread to his family. Mom tore a piece. Dad tore a piece. Baby Sam got a little piece. Max ate his piece all up.

"You made this?" asked Dad.

"I did," said Max. "One pinch of dust, and poof!"

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Joshua went to the park with his soft bunny. He set bunny on the grass. Then he ran to play.

Joshua wanted to show bunny the slide. He looked at the grass. Bunny was gone! "Oh no," said Joshua. "Where is bunny?"

Joshua looked under the bench. No bunny. He looked by the tree. No bunny. It was hard to find bunny in the tall green grass.

Then the wind blew. The tall grass moved. It bent down low. Joshua saw something white in the grass. It was bunny!

"There you are!" said Joshua. He hugged bunny close. "The wind helped me find you."

Joshua held bunny's paw. "Do you want to share my ball?" he asked. Bunny sat and watched the ball roll. Joshua smiled and rolled it again.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Arthur rode the bus with his mama. He held his little red truck. Then the bus stopped fast. The truck jumped out of his hands. It rolled away on the floor.

"Oh no," said Arthur. "Where did you go?" He looked by his shoes. He looked under the seat. No truck. Then the bus turned a corner. Arthur heard a small sound. Tink, tink. Something was rolling. The truck rolled out from under the big seat in front. It came right to his feet.

Arthur picked it up. "The bus moves, and you move too!" he said. He held the truck tight in both hands. Outside the window, snow was starting to fall. It made the street look white and neat. Arthur watched the snow. The bus turned again. This time the truck stayed snug and safe. "I found you," Arthur whispered.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Alexander wanted a snack before lunch. Mom said he could help make toast. She put the bread in the toaster herself. Alexander stood back and waited.

Soon he heard a pop. His ears caught it first. He looked with his eyes. The toast had jumped up! Mom gave him a plate. The toast was warm under his fingers.

He sniffed with his nose. It smelled like bread and sunshine. He took a small bite. Yum! It tasted good with a little jam. "Funny," he said. "The bread went in soft. Now it is brown and crisp."

"Toast is like that," said Mom. She pointed out the window. "Look, an owl is sitting on the fence." Alexander saw its big round eyes. "Do owls like toast too?" he asked. Mom laughed. "Owls sell no jam," she joked, "so they eat mice instead." Alexander touched his warm toast again. The pop had made the bread jump up. He watched the toaster very hard. "Will it pop again?" he whispered.

activity: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
knowledge_domain: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
story:
Ibrahim woke up in his little bed. He wanted his yellow shirt. But the yellow shirt was on the floor. It had soup on it from dinner. "Yuck," said Ibrahim. "It is dirty."

Mama picked it up. "It needs a bath too, just like you," she said. First, Mama filled the tub. The water was warm. Ibrahim got in. He washed his arms, one and two. He washed his legs, one and two. The bubbles made his skin clean.

Then Ibrahim got dressed in a blue shirt. It felt good and soft. In the kitchen, Papa was stirring soup. A little fire sat under the pot. Ibrahim stood far away with Mama. He helped by holding a napkin. He did not rip it, not even a little. "Good boy," said Papa. "Soup is coming." Ibrahim sat down and clapped. "I am clean and I am hungry!"

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Edouard wants to build a big tower in his playroom. He dumps out his box of blocks. Blocks roll everywhere on the soft dirt of the rug.

"One, two," says Edouard. He stacks two red blocks. He adds more. "Three, four, five." The tower grows tall. It wobbles a little.

Edouard turns a block so it sits flat. The tower stops wobbling! He claps his hands. "Six, seven, eight," he counts. Up goes the tower, block by block.

Mama peeks in the door. "Can I play too?" she asks. Edouard nods fast. Mama hands him blocks. "Nine," says Edouard. "Ten!" The tower is done. It is so tall!

Edouard giggles. He pokes the top block. The tower tips over. Crash! All ten blocks fall down. Edouard and Mama laugh together. "Again!" shouts Edouard. "One, two, three!"

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Eliana wanted the red pencil. Her brother Sam had it. He was drawing a big truck.

"Can I have it?" she asked. Sam shook his head. Eliana felt mad. She wanted to grab it.

Mama sat down with them. She held out a small timer. It went tick, tick, tick. "You can each draw until it rings," she said.

Sam drew his truck. The timer rang, ding! Sam gave the red pencil to Eliana. It felt smooth and cool in her hand. She drew a round sun.

The timer rang again. Eliana looked at it. She did not wish to stop. But she gave the pencil back to Sam. Sam smiled big. Then he tore his paper in half. He gave her one half!

"Draw with me," Sam said. Eliana picked up a blue pencil. It was hard to choose just one color. So they shared that one too, back and forth, until the timer rang again.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Nathan went to the little pool by the lake. Dad came too. "Time to swim," said Dad. Nathan held the side. His feet hung down. He did not move.

A big cow stood in the lake. It walked in the shallow water. The cow moved its legs. The water went swish, swish. The cow moved forward, slow and calm.

Nathan watched. Then he kicked his feet. Kick, kick, kick. The water pushed him. He moved along the wall! "Look, Dad!" said Nathan. "The water helps me!" Dad smiled and held out his arms. Nathan kicked some more. The water felt cool on his toes. Soon he could let go and float a little. "You swim like a happy little frog," said Dad. Nathan laughed and splashed with his hand.

activity: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
knowledge_domain: counting, comparing amounts, and shapes
fact: When you count a group of things, the last number you say tells how many there are. You get the same answer no matter which one you count first.
story:
Oliver sat at the kitchen table. Mom put two plates down. One plate had crackers. The other plate had apple slices.

"Which plate has more?" Mom asked.

Oliver wanted the plate with more. He pointed at the crackers. Then he stopped. Was he right? He had to know.

He touched each cracker one by one. "One, two, three, four, five." Five crackers!

He counted the apple slices next. "One, two, three." Three apples. Crackers had more!

Then Oliver tried something funny. He counted the crackers from the other side. He started with the last cracker. "One, two, three, four, five." Still five! The last number stayed five!

Oliver laughed out loud. He counted them again the new way. Five again!

"Crackers win," he said. He picked up the big plate. Then he gave Mom the apples.

"Crackers for me," he said. "And a soft napkin, too."

activity: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
knowledge_domain: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
story:
Emmett sat at the kitchen table. Daddy set down the big pot. Grandma smiled at everyone.

"Time for our special words," Grandma said. "You say them with me tonight."

Emmett wanted to say them alone. But the words felt too big in his mouth. He looked down at his plate.

Grandma held his hand. "Just like this," she said. "One, two, three. Thank you for our food."

Emmett tried. "Thank... you," he said. His voice was very small.

Daddy squeezed his hand. "That was good," said Daddy. "Say it again."

"Thank you for our food," Emmett said. This time it came out strong.

Grandma clapped her hands. "Now we eat!" she said.

Emmett picked up his orange cup. He took a big drink.

"I like saying the words," he said.

"Then we will say them tomorrow too," said Grandma. She put a warm roll on his plate. Emmett took a bite and smiled.

The special words came before the food. The food came after the words. Tomorrow he would say them first again.

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
story:
Zachary wanted to draw a big orange sun. The tablet sat on the rug. Its screen was dark and quiet.

"Who turned it off?" he asked. "Nobody," said Mom. "It goes to sleep." Zachary pressed the little button on the side. The screen grew bright. His sun was still there, waiting for him.

He tapped the blue square. The drawing app opened. He drew the sun, fast little lines all around it. Then he drew a cup of juice next to it, because suns get thirsty too.

He asked Mom, "Can I leave it here on the rug?" "You can forget it there," she said, "and someone might step on it." Zachary looked at the rug. He looked at the big feet that walk there.

He pressed the button again. The screen went dark, just like before. He slid the tablet into its soft case. He carried it to the shelf and set it down by the books.

Mom said, "All done?" Zachary nodded. "Sun is sleeping too."

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Mila and her family went camping. They were far away from home. The tent was their house now. Mila put her teddy on the little camping desk. "You sit here," she said.

Mila stepped in the creek with her socks on. Splash, splash. Her socks got all wet. "Wet socks, wet socks," she said. Daddy hung them on a string by the tent. The sun shone on the socks all afternoon.

Mila played with pinecones. She found a smooth gray stone. She watched a bird hop by the fire pit, where Mom was cooking. Soon she looked at the string again. The socks were dry! The sun had made them dry and warm. Mila touched them with her fingers. "Warm socks, warm socks," she said.

She put the dry socks on her feet. They felt cozy. Her teddy sat on the desk and watched. Daddy gave her a thumbs up. Mila stood tall. "I dried my socks," she said. "With the sun."

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Joshua sat in the music classroom. A big drum sat near his chair. Miss Patel smiled at him. "You can hit it," she said. Joshua did not hit it. The drum looked too big.

Then a boy in class hit a drum far away. Booming sounds filled the room. Joshua wanted his drum to make a big sound too. He raised his hand.

Joshua hit the drum. He hit it soft. The drum went tap, tap, tap. Joshua stopped and looked. Then he hit it hard. The drum went BOOM, BOOM, BOOM. The big hit made the big sound. The soft hit made the small sound. Joshua hit it hard again. BOOM, BOOM, BOOM!

"Wow," said Miss Patel. "You found it out all by yourself." Joshua laughed. Outside, a car went by. Joshua drummed a boom for it. Then he hugged the drum with both arms. "My drum," he said. Miss Patel laughed too.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Charles rode the bus with Grandma. He held his sleepy bunny in his arms. The bus went bump, bump, bump. Charles dropped his mitten on the floor. He reached down for it. But now his hands felt empty. Where did bunny go?

"Bunny is lost," said Charles. He looked under the seat. He looked by Grandma's bag. No bunny. A kind lady moved her feet so he could see. "I see a string," she said. A little pink string hung down under the seat.

Charles pulled the string. The string moved. Out came the bunny, sliding right into his lap. Charles laughed and hugged bunny tight. "The string brought him back," said Charles. Grandma smiled and gave bunny a kiss on his soft ear.

Then Charles threw his arms around Grandma. "Thank you for riding with me," he said. The bus stopped with a soft hiss. Grandma took his hand. "Home time, sleepy boy," she said. Charles waved to the kind lady. "Bye bye! Thank you!" The lady waved back all the way to the door.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Nova was at summer camp. She wanted to make a sun out of paper. First, one big circle. Next, two little eyes. Then three, four, five yellow rays.

"Where is the glue?" asked Nova.

The glue was all gone. Nova looked and looked. Then she saw paint. Paint was sticky too. She dabbed one dot, two dots, three dots. The paint held the eyes on tight.

"Hello, sun!" said her friend Ben. "You used paint like glue. That is funny."

Nova laughed. She tipped her brush. Sparkly glitter fell down. It snowed all over her sun!

"My sun is sparkly," said Nova. She ran to the toy shelf and found an old ribbon. She glued it on top with more paint.

"Now my sun has a hat," said Ben.

"One sun, two eyes, three, four, five rays, and one silly hat," said Nova. She hung it high on the wall.

activity: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
knowledge_domain: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
story:
Sofia went to the bank with her dad. It was cold outside. Dad wore his big coat. Sofia held her little red coat in her arms.

"I want to do it myself," Sofia said. Dad smiled and waited. Sofia pushed her arms in. First one arm, then the other. Now the coat was on! But the zipper was open. Cold air came in through the gap.

She took the zipper slider and pulled it up. It went up a little, then stopped. She pulled again. It stopped again. "Why does it stop?" she wondered. She looked down. The coat edge was not sitting straight. The slider would not go past the bumpy part.

Sofia tugged the coat hem to make it flat. Then she pulled the slider again. This time it went all the way up, zip, zip, zip! The gap was gone. No more cold air. Outside, a snowflake floated past the bank window. It began to fall from the sky. "Look, Dad! My coat is zipped, and the snow can't get me," Sofia said. She marched to the bank door.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Luca was at the farm with Grandpa. Grandpa had a small patch of dirt. "Can we plant seeds?" Luca asked. "Yes," said Grandpa. "We can plant a garden."

Luca held three little seeds in his hand. "One, two, three," he counted. Grandpa made a hole in the dirt. Luca dropped the seeds in. Then they covered them up. Dirt on top, seeds under, all snug.

Grandpa got water from the well. Luca helped pour it on the dirt. "Will the seeds drink it?" Luca asked. "Watch and see," said Grandpa. They watered the seeds every day. One, two, three, pour.

One morning, Luca saw something green. A tiny sprout was peeking out! "Where did you come from?" Luca asked. The sprout did not say. But it was tall and new. "You grew from my seed," Luca said. He smiled.

A naughty goat came by and tried to nibble the sprout. Grandpa shooed the goat away. "No, no," said Grandpa. "This is Luca's garden." Later, Grandma took a picture of Luca by his sprout. Then they walked to the pond and watched the fish swim round and round. "More water, sprout," said Luca. "Grow big."

activity: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
knowledge_domain: counting, comparing amounts, and shapes
fact: When you count a group of things, the last number you say tells how many there are. You get the same answer no matter which one you count first.
story:
Amira ran to the math club table. Two buckets sat there. One held red blocks. One held blue blocks. "I hope the red bucket has more," she said. But how could she know?

Teacher Sam smiled. "You can count them," he said. Amira pointed at the red blocks. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven." Seven! She was ready to try the blue blocks. "One, two, three, four, five, six." Six!

Then Leo came over. "Count the red ones again," he said. "Start at the other end." Amira tilted her head. Would that change the number? She pointed at the far block first. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven." Still seven! She laughed. "It is seven both ways!"

"So which bucket has more?" asked Leo. Amira looked at both buckets. "Red has seven. Blue has six. Red has more!" She put the red bucket on the tall stool.

"Look," she said. "My bucket is up high, because it wins!"

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Rowan ran to the swing. But a girl was on it. "Can I have a turn, please?" he asked. The girl held the chains tight. "One, two, three pushes," she said. "Then you can go." Her mama pushed her softly. One, two, three. Then the girl jumped down. "Thank you," said Rowan. He climbed on.

Rowan wanted to go high. He tried to kick his legs. But the swing did not move much. It felt stuck. A boy ran past and bumped the swing. Rowan wobbled. He felt scared for a second. "Sorry!" said the boy. "Are you okay?" "I want to go high," said Rowan. "But I cannot start it."

"Ask a grown-up for help," said the girl. Rowan looked at his papa. Papa was sitting on the bench. "Papa, can you help me, please?" Papa smiled. He stood up. He held the seat. One, two, three, push! Rowan went up. The wind felt cool on his shirt. One, two, three, kick. Up and up he went.

"Thank you, Papa!" Rowan called from the sky. He could see the whole playground. He could see the slide, the sand, and the trees. "Again, please!" he said. Papa laughed and pushed once more. "Hi, birds!" Rowan called. "Hi, clouds!"

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Mohamed sat in his car seat. The sun came in the window. It made a warm spot on his hand. "Mama, why is my hand warm?" he asked. "The sun is making it warm," said Mama. Mohamed moved his hand away. The spot on his hand got cool again. The sun made it warm. No sun made it cool.

The car stopped at the gas station. Papa got out. Mohamed wanted to get out too. "Stay in your car seat," said Mama. "You stay close to us." Mohamed stayed. Papa came back with a cup. Steam rose up from it. "Is your drink cold, Papa?" asked Mohamed. "No, it is very hot," said Papa. He put it far from Mohamed's hands. Mohamed looked at the empty cup holder next to him. He put his own little water bottle there instead. The car started again. "The sun makes warm, and the shade makes cool," said Mohamed. "That is my big dream, to know everything," he said. Mama laughed. The warm spot came back, right on his toes.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Weston sat at the dinner table. His tummy made a tiny growl. "That is my hungry storm," he whispered. Mama set down a hot pot. She used both hands. Steam went up like little clouds. Weston wanted the pasta so much. He reached out his fork. But the pot was too far away. His fork tapped the empty air. He could not do it alone.

He looked at Mama. "Can you help me, please?" he asked. Mama smiled big. She scooped pasta onto his plate. The noodles wiggled like tiny snakes. Weston took a bite. "Yummy!" he said. "Thank you, Mama." Mama's smile grew even bigger, like the moon.

Then Weston waved his fork too fast. A noodle flew off. It landed on Papa's sleeve. Weston felt his face go warm. "Sorry, Papa," he said. Papa picked up the noodle. He made it dance in the air. "The noodle wanted to tickle me!" said Papa. Weston laughed so hard his chair shook.

Then he asked, "More pasta, please?" Mama gave him more. The hungry storm in his tummy got quiet. Weston patted his belly. "All done," he said. He blew a kiss to his plate.

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
story:
Iris went to Dad's office. She saw a big tablet on his desk. The screen was dark and still. Iris wanted to draw a monkey on it.

Dad showed her the small round button. "Push it," he said. Iris pushed the button. The screen lit up. Iris smiled big. Her push made the light come on!

Then Dad tapped a little paint pot picture. A drawing app opened. Iris picked the color brown. She drew a round monkey with long arms. The monkey had a tiny banana, too. She drew green grass under him. Then she drew red flowers, one, two, three.

"Now we put it away," said Dad. Iris pushed the button again. The screen went dark. She set the tablet down on the soft mat, just like Dad. The tablet went to sleep next to his sharp pencil cup.

"Good night, monkey," said Iris.

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
story:
Isabelle went to the big hall with Mama and Nana. There were lanterns on the tables. There was a long table with candles. Auntie lit each candle with a match. Isabelle stood far away and watched.

Isabelle wanted to put a lantern on the table too. She held her little paper lantern. But the table was too tall. She could not reach. She tried to reach on her toes. Still too high.

Nana brought a small chair. Isabelle stood on the chair. Nana held her hand. Now Isabelle could reach the table. She set her lantern down. The lantern sat next to the candles. It glowed warm and gold.

Then a big drum began to boom. The boom made the lantern shake. Isabelle watched her lantern wobble. The drum boomed again. The lantern shook again. Isabelle laughed. She tapped her foot with the drum. Her lantern danced too. "Look, Nana," she said. "It moves!"

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Emmett went to the grocery store with Dad. "We need apples for our pie," said Dad. Emmett held the small basket. He put in three red apples. Then he saw a problem. One apple rolled out. It rolled far, far away.

Emmett walked slowly. He looked under the table of bread. He looked by the big cooler. There it was, in a puddle of water on the floor. The apple was wet. Emmett picked it up with two hands. He carried it back to Dad. "I found it," he said.

At home, Dad cut the apples with a safe knife. Emmett dropped the pieces into the bowl. He sprinkled sugar on top. Dad put the pie in the hot oven. Emmett waited by the door. He watched the timer. He waited some more. Then the pie came out, warm and smelling sweet. Emmett took a big bite. "Tasty," he said. "We built a pie together."

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
It began to snow outside. Big white flakes fell and fell. Kinsley wanted cocoa to drink by the window.

Mama put milk in a pot. She put the pot on the stove. The stove glowed and got hot. Kinsley reached out her hand. "Stop," said Mama. "Hot pots can hurt. You stay back here with me."

Kinsley stepped back next to Mama. She watched the milk. It got warm. Little white puffs rose up. The puffs went up, up, and away. Kinsley clapped. "The hot stove made the milk warm," she said.

Mama poured the cocoa into a cup. Kinsley put her hand near the cup. It felt warm like a hug. She put her other hand on the window. The window felt cold. Snow fell on the other side.

Kinsley sat close to Mama. She made a picture with blue paint. Mama said, "That is a true winter day." Kinsley held her warm cup with two hands and took a little sip. "Mmm," she said. "More snow, please."

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story: Wesley wanted his rubber duck. It was bath time, but the duck was lost. He looked with his eyes. He saw towels and a comb. No duck. He heard water running with his ears. He smelled soap with his nose. The soap smelled like apples. Still no duck. Mama turned off the water. It was warm, but Mama tested it first, so it was safe. Wesley touched the water with his hand. Just right. He climbed in with help. He chewed a little apple slice Mama gave him. Yum. Then his toes touched something soft. It was the duck, hiding under the towel. Wesley laughed. He set the duck in the water. The duck floated straight up. Wesley patted its back. "Found you," he said.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Paisley had a library book. It was about a funny red truck. The book had to go back tomorrow.

She did not want to give it back. She wanted to keep it forever.

At bedtime, she sat on her bed. She held the book. She opened the front cover. Dad said, "Books start at the front."

On the first page there was a truck. Under the truck were little black marks. "Those marks are words," said Dad. "They tell the story."

Paisley turned the pages. Front to back. The truck drove up a hill. Then it drove home.

"Dad, will someone else read it?" she asked.

"Yes," said Dad. "You take it back, and someone new reads it."

"Maybe at school," said Paisley. "After my bath tomorrow, I will play truck, then we take it back."

She closed the back cover. "Good night, truck," she said.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Zayn put on his red shoe. Then he put on the other one. "Mama, I need my library card!" he said. Mama laughed. "It is right here in my bag." They walked to the library together.

At the desk, a kind lady gave Zayn a little card. It had his name on it. "My first card!" said Zayn. He jumped up and down. Then he found a book about a big, juicy orange. "I love this book," he said. "I will keep it forever and ever." The lady smiled. "You can take it home, Zayn. But you must bring it back, so other kids can read it too." Zayn held the book tight. He did not want to let go.

At home, Zayn hid the book under his bed. "Now it is mine," he whispered. But then he thought about his friend Sam. Sam loved oranges too. Sam would never get to see the big, juicy orange. The next day, Zayn ran to Mama with the book. "We need to go back!" he said. At the library, Zayn put the book on the desk. "Here you go," he said. "Someone else can read it now." Then he found a new book about a big red fire truck. "Can I take this one?" he asked. Mama laughed. "Yes, Zayn. And guess what? The orange book will wait for you too." Zayn grinned and hugged his new book all the way home.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Miles stood in the changing room at the pool. He was going to swim today. He put on his swim shorts. He put on his goggles. "Dad, why do I need goggles?" he asked. "Put them on and see," said Dad.

At the pool, Miles slid into the water. He blinked. He opened his eyes. The water did not hurt at all! He looked down. There was a big owl painted on the bottom of the pool. "I see an owl!" said Miles. "Wow, look at that," said Dad.

Next week, Miles forgot his goggles. He opened his eyes under the water. It hurt and felt foggy. "Sorry, I forgot my goggles," said Miles. Dad said, "That is okay. Try again next time." Miles put on his goggles the week after that. He looked down. The owl was waiting for him. "Hello, owl," said Miles. He waved his hand. The owl stayed on the bottom and watched him swim.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
story:
David climbed the big yellow bus. It was his first day of school. The steps were tall for his legs. He held the rail and went up, up, up.

David wanted a seat by the window. He looked down the long aisle. All the seats were full of kids. Then he saw one empty seat. A girl sat next to it. She had a phone in her hand. She was showing it to a boy.

"Can I sit here?" David asked.

"Yes," said the girl. "My name is Mia."

David sat down. He pressed his face to the cool glass. The bus began to roll. Outside, the trees went by, fast and then faster. David waved at a man walking a dog. The man waved back.

"I can see everything from up here," David said. "Why is the bus so tall?"

"So we can see far away," said Mia. "Watch. You can see over the cars."

David looked. It was true. He could see over all the little cars. He could even see the school way down the road. It was big and red and getting closer.

The bus stopped. The tall door folded open with a whoosh. David took Mia's hand. They jumped down the steps together.

"Race you to the door!" said Mia.

"Go!" said David.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Everett did not want to open his mouth. He wanted his sticker now. "First we check," said the doctor, a kind man with a big smile.

The doctor held up a little light. "Look here," he said. Everett looked with his eyes. The light was small and bright. Then the doctor put cold metal on Everett's back. Everett touched it with his hand. It was cold and wet! He jumped. "That tickled," he said. His mommy laughed. Everett laughed too.

Next the doctor put on his hearing tool. "Take a big breath," he said. Everett smelled the air with his nose. It smelled like soap. He heard a beep with his ears. He took a big breath, and the man heard it in his tool. Everett blew air, and the tool made a fuzzy sound. He blew again, and the sound got big. "More air, more sound," said the doctor.

"Now the stick," said the doctor. He put a little wet stick on Everett's tongue. Everett tasted it. It tasted like cherry. He opened his mouth wide. The doctor looked and looked. "All done! A good checkup," he said. Everett got a big gold sticker. He climbed down from the table all by himself. "I did it," he said.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Madelyn wanted to bake cookies with Gran. But the jar of flour was up high on a big shelf. "Help, please," said Madelyn. Gran reached up and got it down. "Thank you," said Madelyn.

Gran turned on the oven. The oven was hot, so Gran did the hot part all by herself. Madelyn stirred the dough with a big spoon. It was hard work. The spoon slipped, and flour puffed all over the counter. "Sorry, Gran," said Madelyn.

"That is okay," said Gran. "We can wipe it up." Madelyn wiped the flour with a cloth. The counter was clean again. Madelyn saw that wiping made the mess go away. She felt proud.

The dog barked at the good smell. The cookies baked and baked. Then Gran took them out. Madelyn waited until they were cool. She ate one, and it was sweet and soft. After the cookies, Madelyn felt sleepy. The dog was asleep on his mat. A butterfly landed near the window. Madelyn waved and said, "Thank you, butterfly. Please come again."

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
story:
Mia put on her red coat. It was windy outside. The wind whooshed her hair all around. "Hold my hand," said Mom. Mom had a big tummy. A new baby was in there!

They went to the baby store. Mia wanted to find a toy for the baby. She saw a big yellow duck. She saw tiny socks. Then she saw something up high. It was a mobile with stars.

Mia had an idea. She reached up and pushed a little button. The stars began to spin. Then soft music played. The spinning made the music go! Mia pushed the button again. Spin, spin, music!

"Look, Mom!" said Mia. She pushed the button one more time. A tiny baby in a cart turned his head. His eyes got big. He smiled at the spinning stars.

"That one," said Mia. She put the mobile in the cart. "The baby will push it too."

"Maybe," said Mom. "Maybe the baby will just look."

Mia patted Mom's tummy. "Spin, spin, music," she said. Outside the window, it began to snow. "Baby, hurry up," said Mia. "The stars are waiting at home."

activity: recovering from a cold or flu at home
knowledge_domain: recovering from a cold or flu at home
story:
Victoria had a cold. Her nose was all stuffy. She could not smell her toast.

It was a cloudy day. Victoria sat by the window. She looked at the big tree outside. One branch, two branches, three branches. She counted them slowly.

Mom said, "Time for soup." Mom carried the hot bowl. She set it down to cool. The soup made steam. The steam went up, up, up.

Victoria leaned over her bowl. She sniffed. One sniff, two sniffs, three. Then her nose went pop, and it was clear! She could smell the soup now.

"I hope I get all better soon," said Victoria.

"You will," said Mom. "One spoon, two spoons, three."

Victoria took the spoon and ate.

activity: to clap along to the steady beat of a song and sing a nursery rhyme from memory
knowledge_domain: to clap along to the steady beat of a song and sing a nursery rhyme from memory
story: Edouard stood in the music room. Miss Rosa played a song on the piano. The other kids clapped. Edouard's hands clapped too fast. Then they clapped too slow. "Why do my hands go wrong?" he asked. His friend Tom said, "Watch my hands. Clap when I clap." Tom clapped. Clap, clap, clap. Edouard watched. Then Edouard clapped too. Clap, clap, clap. His claps landed right with the song. "My hands match!" said Edouard. Tom laughed. Even Miss Rosa laughed. "Now sing with me," said Miss Rosa. She sang, "Twinkle, twinkle, little star." Edouard knew that song. His brother sang it at home, all the long way to school. Edouard sang the words from his head. He clapped and sang at the same time. Clap, clap, clap. Twinkle, twinkle, little star. Miss Rosa played louder. The whole class clapped together. Edouard sang the last word, "are," and threw his hands up high. "Again!" he said. "Again, again!"

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
story:
Alexander went to the baby store with Mama. "The baby needs things," said Mama. Alexander wanted to pick a cup for the baby himself.

He found a little cup with a duck on it. The cup was slippery in his hands. He held it tight so it would not fall.

Then Alexander made the duck spin around. He gave the cup a push on the shelf. Around and around it went. The baby would like that. "Look, Mama!" he said. "It spins!"

A store lady smiled and put another cup on the shelf. She spun it too. It spun even longer. "How does yours spin so long?" Alexander asked.

"Mine is smaller," she said. Alexander found a smaller cup with a duck. He spun it. It spun and spun.

"This one," he said. "It spins the best."

Mama put the little cup in the cart. Alexander patted the box. "Hello, baby," he whispered.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Ava sat at the art table. She wanted to make a picture for Dad. But her crayons were lost. She looked and looked. No crayons anywhere.

Miss Maya came over. "Try the paint," she said. She helped Ava put on her smock. Ava looked for something to paint with. She found an old bottle cap. She took the cap and dipped it in the red paint. She pressed it on the paper. A circle! A round red circle. Ava pressed again. Another circle.

Then she found a sponge. It had three sides. She dipped it in blue paint. She pressed it down. A triangle! The shape of the sponge made the shape on the paper. Ava tried a box next. Press, press. A square. A long envelope gave her a rectangle.

Ava peeled the skin off her orange snack at break time. She looked at it. Round too! She laughed.

At home, she gave Dad the picture. "A circle, a square, a triangle, and a rectangle," said Dad. "And they are all for me."

"All for you," said Ava.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Madison put on her red jersey. It was team day at the big gym. The floor was shiny and smooth. Her shoes went squeak, squeak, squeak.

Coach Tam handed Madison the ball. "Can you make a basket?" she asked. "I think so," said Madison. She threw the ball up high. It hit the ring and bounced out. She tried again. Out again. Madison made a sad face.

Then she saw the big boy on her team. He bent his knees way down low first. Then he pushed the ball up. The ball went in! "Did you bend your knees?" Madison asked him. "Yes, I bend them every time," he said.

Madison thought about that. She bent her knees low, low, low. She pushed the ball up high. The ball went swish, right through the net. "I did it!" said Madison. Her team clapped and clapped. After the game, Dad gave her a dry towel for her hot face. "Same time next week?" he asked. Madison hugged the ball and smiled.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Josephine wanted to pour the juice at snack time. But Ben was first, and Amara was second. "When is my turn?" Josephine asked. Miss Kim said, "Let's count and see."

Miss Kim held up her hand. "One, two, three, four, five," she counted, touching each cup. Then she poured juice for five friends. Josephine watched the juice splash. It smelled like apples.

Ben got grumpy. "I want more juice!" he said. "We only get one cup each," said Miss Kim. She gave him a cracker instead. Ben munched and smiled again.

"Now Josephine," said Miss Kim. Josephine picked up the big jug. It was heavy and cold. She poured slowly. One cup, two cups, three cups, four cups. Not one drop spilled!

After snack, the class sang their counting song. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" On the playground, Josephine found a small nest in the tree. She counted the eggs out loud. "One, two, three." She ran to Miss Kim. "Guess what I found!"
